(Rock Island, Illinois) | college = [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State]] (2015–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | career_start = 2019 | years1 = [[2019–20 NBA G League season|2019]]–[[2021–22 NBA G League season|2022]] | team1 = [[Westchester Knicks]] | years2 = {{nbay|2021|start}} | team2 = [[New York Knicks]] | years3 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022]]–[[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = [[Texas Legends]] | highlights = * 2× First-team All-[[Big Sky Conference|Big Sky]] (2017, 2019) }} '''Tyler Jordan Hall''' (born March 25, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Montana State Bobcats men's basketball|Montana State Bobcats]]. ==High school career== Hall attended [[Rock Island High School]]. He was named the 2014–15 Dispatch/Argus Metro boys' basketball co-player of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Wendland |first1=Jeff |title=Rock Island grad Tyler Hall picked 4th in G-League |url=https://qconline.com/sports/basketball/professional/rock-island-grad-tyler-hall-picked-th-in-g-league/article_b4424dad-db9e-56e2-93da-585355e8c945.html#37 |accessdate=November 13, 2019 |work=Rock Island Dispatch-Argus |date=October 27, 2019}} Hall was twice named to the All-State team but was lightly recruited out of high school.{{cite news |last1=Meenan |first1=Jim |title=Motivated Tyler Hall proving he belongs as D-I star at Montana State |url=https://qctimes.com/sports/basketball/college/motivated-tyler-hall-proving-he-belongs-as-d-i-star/article_1f1894d5-234e-5671-8ba1-66803560eec9.html |accessdate=November 14, 2019 |work=Quad Cities Times |date=June 12, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman, Hall averaged 18.6 points per game and was named Big Sky Freshman of the Year.{{cite press release|url=http://www.bigskyconf.com/news/2016/3/7/MBB_0307163753.aspx |title=Bolomboy Named Big Sky Men's Basketball MVP, Defensive Player Of The Year |publisher=Big Sky Conference |date=March 7, 2016 |accessdate=March 7, 2016}} Hall had a career-high 42 points in a game against [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]] on December 5, 2016. He posted 23.1 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game as a sophomore. Hall was named to the First-team All-[[Big Sky Conference]].{{cite press release|url=http://www.bigskyconf.com/news/2017/3/6/MBB_0306175634.aspx |title=Wiley Headlines 2016–17 #BIGSKYMBB All-Conference Team |publisher=Big Sky Conference |date=March 6, 2017 |accessdate=March 6, 2017}} As a junior, Hall averaged 17.5 points and 7.7 rebounds per game. He declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but decided to return to school.{{cite news |last1=Schwedelson |first1=Paul |title=Hall joins Chicago Bulls' Summer League roster |url=https://www.bozemandailychronicle.com/sports/bobcats/mens-basketball/hall-joins-chicago-bulls-summer-league-roster/article_37e09662-a7aa-55e5-b0ad-4eaed2fa8b37.html |accessdate=November 14, 2019 |work=[[Bozeman Daily Chronicle]] |date=June 24, 2019}} Hall eclipsed the 2,000-point mark in an 81–76 win over [[North Dakota Fighting Hawks men's basketball|North Dakota]].{{cite news|last1=Rachac|first1=Greg|title=Tyler Hall on cusp of Montana State scoring record as team preps for Pac-12 Washington State|url=https://missoulian.com/sports/college/big-sky-conference/montana-state-university/tyler-hall-on-cusp-of-montana-state-scoring-record-as/article_ad650b2b-30fe-592c-97db-32683b782f33.html|accessdate=December 8, 2018|work=[[Missoulian]]|date=November 28, 2018}} As a senior, Hall averaged 20.5 points, 2.8 assists and 4.7 rebounds per game. He was named to the First-team All-Big Sky Conference. He ranks ninth all-time in 3-pointers made in Division I basketball with 431.{{cite web |last1=Petraccione |first1=Nick |title=Former Montana State Bobcat Tyler Hall works out with Chicago Bulls |url=https://www.montanasports.com/cat-griz/montana-state-bobcats/2019/06/12/tyler-hall-works-out-with-chicago-bulls/ |website=Montana Sports |accessdate=November 14, 2019 |date=June 13, 2019}} Hall finished his career with 2,518 points, breaking the Big Sky Conference record of held by [[Eastern Washington Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Washington]]'s [[Bogdan Bliznyuk]].{{cite news |title=Ex-Montana State guard Tyler Hall picked fourth in NBA G League draft |url=https://helenair.com/sports/college/big-sky-conference/montana-state-university/ex-montana-state-guard-tyler-hall-picked-fourth-in-nba/article_16153909-beb3-5bbb-857d-4029d0fba770.html |accessdate=November 13, 2019 |work=[[Helena Independent Record]] |date=October 26, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===Westchester / New York Knicks (2019–2022)=== Hall participated in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] with the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He was selected fourth overall in the [[2019 NBA G League draft]] by the [[Westchester Knicks]]. In January 2020, he averaged 12.3 points and 4.0 rebounds per game.{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Wendland|title=Tyler Hall hopes to take his job from G-League to NBA|url=https://qconline.com/sports/basketball/tyler-hall-hopes-to-take-his-job-from-g-league/article_429e8590-cd71-5465-9bb3-dc358f28d55d.html|work=Rock Island Dispatch-Argus|date=February 4, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}} On the season, he averaged 9.3 points and 3.4 rebounds per game, and his 91 three-pointers were second most for a Westchester rookie.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Priczak|title=2019–20 Westchester Knicks Season Recap: Tyler Hall|url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2020/3/31/21198453/2019-20-westchester-knicks-season-recap-tyler-hall|website=Ridiculous Upside|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=March 31, 2020|access-date=May 9, 2020}} On December 12, 2020, Hall was signed by the [[New York Knicks]],{{cite tweet|user=NY_KnicksPR|number=1337920335367327749|date=December 12, 2020|title=@nyknicks Sign Tyler Hall}} and then waived on December 14.{{cite tweet|user=NY_KnicksPR|number=1338648997255389184|date=December 14, 2020|title=New York Knicks announced today that the team has waived guard Tyler Hall.}} He rejoined the Westchester Knicks and averaged 10.1 points, 4.1 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game in the 2020–21 season. In August 2021, Hall joined the New York Knicks for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]]{{cite news|first=Parker|last=Cotton|title=Former Montana State player Tyler Hall makes New York Knicks Summer League team|url=https://406mtsports.com/college/big-sky-conference/montana-state-university/former-montana-state-player-tyler-hall-makes-new-york-knicks-summer-league-team/article_6c2463b8-f689-58be-bbb1-b3ab9c2cf09e.html|work=[[Bozeman Chronicle]]|publisher=406 MT Sports|date=August 2, 2021|access-date=September 26, 2021}} and on October 8, he signed with them.{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Tyler Hall|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-tyler-hall|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 8, 2021|access-date=October 8, 2021}} However, he was waived by the Knicks near the end of training camp.{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Myles Powell|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-myles-powell-0|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 12, 2021|access-date=October 12, 2021}} In October 2021, Hall was included on the training camp roster of the Westchester Knicks.{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce Training Camp Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-training-camp-roster/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 1, 2021}} In 11 games, he averaged 14.6 points, 4.2 rebounds and 3.2 assists over 38.5 minutes.{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Tyler Hall to a 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-tyler-hall-10-day-contract|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=December 18, 2021|access-date=December 18, 2021}} On December 18, 2021, Hall signed a 10-day contract with the [[New York Knicks]] and made his lone [[NBA]] appearance to date, playing two minutes on Christmas Eve against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. Following the expiration of his 10-day contract, he was reacquired and activated by Westchester on January 2, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=2021–22 NBA G League Transactions|date=January 2, 2022|access-date=January 2, 2022}} In the first game of the regular season, Hall posted 31 points, 6 assists and 5 rebounds in a 127–108 loss to the [[Grand Rapids Gold]].{{cite web |title=GOLD WIN AGAINST KNICKS TO KICK OFF REGULAR SEASON |url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20220105/WESGRG/ |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=January 6, 2022 |date=January 5, 2022}} ===Texas Legends (2022–2024)=== In September 2022, Hall was signed by the [[Dallas Mavericks]],{{Cite web|title=Mavericks fill out training camp roster with five signees|url=https://www.mavs.com/camp-signees-2/|access-date=September 21, 2022|website=mavs.com}} but was waived on October 13.{{Cite web|title=Mavs Waive Tyler Hall, DJ Stewart, Marcus Bingham, Mouhamadou Gueye|url=https://hoopswire.com/mavs-waive-tyler-hall-dj-stewart-marcus-bingham-mouhamadou-gueye/|access-date=October 13, 2022|website=hoopswire.com}} He later signed with the [[Texas Legends]] and was named to their opening night roster on November 3.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-announce-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895504|title=Legends Announce 2022–23 Opening Night
